rules.constraint: Do not keep changing only the test when the implementation underfills the bit array by using too many bits, too many hashes, or dropping keys during upgrade.
rules.risk: A one-sided probability assertion is correct for upper-bound tests, but a separate source-derived test may still expect the implementation to approximate the requested probability. Very low observed rates often indicate that constructor formulas, rounding, upgrade reinsertion, or hash-count derivation diverged from the source.
rules.guidance: When the output prints an observed-minus-expected gap that is negative and large, keep the generated assertion one-sided but inspect the implementation. Check that the source formula for bit count is not rounded up to an extra power of two unless the source masks that way, that hash count uses the same floor/ceil/round rule, that upgrade reinserts every occupied table key without metadata bits, and that add/test use the same hash sequence. Fix those implementation details before reducing workload or relaxing assertions.

rules.title: Repair display and file-load contracts directly
rules.trigger: A parser project passes getters but fails string rendering or a load-from-file error-message assertion.
rules.goal: Fix the public formatting and file validation contract without rewriting the parser that already produced usable entries.
rules.constraint: Do not change parser scanning, value conversion, or getter behavior when the failing assertion is about `Display`, `to_string`, or stable load error text.
rules.risk: A broad parser rewrite can introduce borrow/move compile failures while leaving the visible rendering or file-error mismatch unresolved.
rules.guidance: For display failures, compare the expected text with the formatter contract: key, separator, quoted strings, lowercase booleans, fixed decimal floats, normalized color bytes, and newline placement. For file-loading failures, validate empty names and extensions before opening, then map any read/open failure for an otherwise valid path to the API's stable error message instead of forwarding platform-specific IO text. Keep these as narrow fixes to formatter and file wrapper callables.

rules.title: Dispatch directive records by payload shape
rules.trigger: A directive or record parser reaches a marker but then fails with expected digit, unknown instruction, or unexpected character.
rules.goal: Classify section markers, metadata directives, declarations, and terminators before reading directive-specific operands.
rules.constraint: Do not parse every directive as though it has numeric fields or a declaration payload.
rules.risk: The parser can handle the first declaration but fail when a marker or metadata record is routed through the declaration scanner and tries to read a number where none exists.
rules.guidance: After reading a directive keyword, branch by directive class. Metadata records read free-form payloads up to the terminator, declaration records read type/size/id/name fields, scope markers read their own small fields, and marker-only records consume only the terminator. When the failure says `expected digit`, inspect which directive was active before calling the numeric scanner; the repair is usually to skip or separately handle the marker instead of weakening number parsing.

rules.title: Start table mode small enough to reach upgrade threshold
rules.trigger: A probabilistic membership structure passes insertion checks but fails an assertion that it switched from table mode to bit-array mode after enough inserts.
rules.goal: Preserve the lazy table-to-bit-array state transition from the source implementation.
rules.constraint: Do not preallocate the temporary table from the final bit capacity when the source starts with no table and grows through thresholds.
rules.risk: Inserted keys can remain findable, but the mode transition never happens at the expected count because the table starts too large or the growth condition compares the wrong units.
rules.guidance: Initialize temporary table storage empty when the source does, allocate the first small power-of-two table on first growth, and double until the next growth would reach the final bit-array byte size. The upgrade condition should compare table byte cost against final bit-array bytes, then reinsert existing keys into the bit array. If tests check a mode flag after `n + 1` insertions, fix constructor/growth thresholds rather than membership hashing.

rules.title: Compute metadata before moving owners into struct literals
rules.trigger: A project-level patch fails to compile with a moved owner such as a vector or string used again for length, count, or capacity metadata.
rules.goal: Keep the intended behavioral repair while making the struct construction ownership-correct.
rules.constraint: Do not clone the owner just to recover metadata when a scalar can be computed before the move.
rules.risk: A correct test repair can be rejected repeatedly because the generated struct literal moves a collection and then tries to read its length.
rules.guidance: Before a struct literal that takes ownership of a collection, compute any derived scalar fields into locals, for example `let count = entries.len();`, then move the collection once. Use field init order only for readability; Rust evaluates moved values normally, so later field expressions cannot borrow an earlier moved owner.
keywords: does not implement the copy trait

rules.title: Make borrowed cursor bindings mutable, not double-borrowed
rules.trigger: A repair for a shared reader cursor fails with cannot borrow as mutable or suggests changing a parameter to `mut file: &File`.
rules.goal: Read and seek through the same borrowed cursor with the mutability shape Rust's trait impls expect.
rules.constraint: Do not pass `&mut file` when the helper needs a mutable binding to the borrowed cursor, and do not clone/reopen the cursor to silence mutability errors.
rules.risk: Compile repairs can oscillate between cursor cloning, `&mut &File` borrow errors, and helpers that no longer advance the outer parser.
rules.guidance: For functions that take a shared cursor reference and call `read` or `seek`, use `mut file: &File` in the parameter or `let mut file = file;` locally, then call methods on `file`. Helpers should take `mut f: &File` and be called with `file`, not `&mut file`, unless the helper explicitly expects a different wrapper type.

rules.title: Grow vectors without requiring element Clone
rules.trigger: A repair fails because `Vec::resize` needs the element type to implement Clone.
rules.goal: Extend a vector of non-Clone structs without changing the public type layout.
rules.constraint: Do not add broad Clone derives to public structs solely to satisfy one internal resize call.
rules.risk: Adding Clone to complex structs can be impossible or semantically wrong, while the desired behavior only needs fresh default elements.
rules.guidance: Replace `vec.resize(index + 1, value)` with `resize_with(index + 1, || fresh_value())` or a loop that pushes newly constructed elements until the index exists. This keeps each element independently initialized and avoids requiring Clone on the element type.

rules.title: Repair isolated field diffs narrowly
rules.trigger: A test equality diff shows the translated value already matches except for one public field such as capacity, limit, length, metadata text, or a status flag.
rules.goal: Preserve behavior that already passes and change only the semantic source of the mismatched field.
rules.constraint: Do not rewrite scanner, parser, formatter, or table control flow when the observed failure is isolated to one field.
rules.risk: A broad patch can fix the displayed field but regress earlier parsing or construction behavior, causing the repair loop to roll back and lose the useful narrow change.
rules.guidance: When the failing output shows the same struct shape, entries, count, and values with one differing field, locate the field assignment, local default, or constructor literal that produced the left value. Replace that source with the right-side visible contract and leave surrounding parse order, error handling, storage, and formatting unchanged. If a prior repair changed many branches and the next failure moved earlier in the same test, restore the smaller field-only edit.

rules.title: Replace runtime placeholders with real behavior
rules.trigger: A compiled project fails tests by panicking with not implemented, unimplemented, todo, or another placeholder body.
rules.goal: Treat placeholder panics as incomplete translation work, not as a valid compiled implementation.
rules.constraint: Do not leave placeholder macros or not-implemented panics in callables that are exercised by tests.
rules.risk: The project can compile but fail immediately before reaching the behavioral assertion that would guide the actual repair.
rules.guidance: Find the callable named by the panic location or the candidate context and replace its body using the original C logic and surrounding helpers. If replacing the placeholder exposes a new parse error, unknown directive, or assertion failure, keep that real implementation progress and continue repairing the new behavior instead of restoring the placeholder.

rules.title: Keep one-sided probability repairs through timeout
rules.trigger: A generated probabilistic test is changed from absolute difference to an upper-bound check, then the same test times out or reaches a larger workload.
rules.goal: Continue from the one-sided probability condition and repair only runtime cost or generated workload size.
rules.constraint: Do not roll back to an absolute-value probability check just because the corrected condition no longer fails early.
rules.risk: A correct upper-bound generated test can be discarded because the next failure signature is a timeout, causing later repairs to repeat the same two-sided probability mistake.
rules.guidance: If the original failure printed a negative observed-minus-expected probability gap, keep the generated assertion one-sided: `observed - expected > tolerance`. When the follow-up result is timeout or excessive loop output, either reduce only the generated stress workload to a representative finite set or optimize the membership path. Preserve inserted-key membership checks and do not reintroduce `.abs()` around the probability gap.

rules.title: Do not use buffer limits as returned capacity
rules.trigger: A returned struct equality diff shows only capacity differing, and the wrong value matches a buffer size, max value size, or internal array limit.
rules.goal: Keep semantic capacity separate from token, value, string, or scratch-buffer sizes.
rules.constraint: Do not substitute key length limits, value length limits, fixed array lengths, Vec capacity, or parser scratch sizes for the public capacity field.
rules.risk: A repair can change one wrong capacity default into another internal constant while preserving the same failing assertion.
rules.guidance: If `left.capacity` changes from one internal size to another but `right.capacity` remains a smaller visible literal or public fixture value, the repair is still wrong. Search the constructor and successful return paths for every assignment to the capacity field. Replace the semantic capacity source with the right-side expected value or the interface default that produced it. Constants named like max key, max value, buffer length, line length, or fixed string size are not candidate capacities unless the public interface explicitly uses them as the entry capacity.

rules.title: Trim directive payload text after the directive token
rules.trigger: A parsed metadata field has the right text but includes a leading tab, space, or newline compared with the expected string.
rules.goal: Match scanf-style directive parsing where whitespace in the format consumes any amount of input whitespace before the payload scanset.
rules.constraint: Do not copy indentation that separates a directive token from its payload into the public metadata string.
rules.risk: The parser reaches the correct directive and copies the correct bytes, but equality fails because indentation became part of date, version, unit, title, or other metadata.
rules.guidance: For text directives with a keyword followed by a free-form payload until a terminator marker or newline, skip leading ASCII whitespace after the directive token before starting the public payload buffer. Then read until the source terminator, trim only terminator text and trailing whitespace that the C scanset excludes, and store the resulting payload. Preserve meaningful internal spaces inside the payload; only separator whitespace before the first payload byte should be removed.

rules.title: Keep probability generated tests one-sided and finite
rules.trigger: A generated probabilistic test first fails because a lower false-positive rate is treated as bad, then the one-sided repair times out on a large stress loop.
rules.goal: Preserve the source's upper-bound probability contract while keeping generated validation within the normal test timeout.
rules.constraint: Do not restore absolute-difference checks just because the corrected generated test runs longer; fix the generated workload or implementation cost instead.
rules.risk: After removing `.abs()`, the harness can stop failing early and expose an overly large generated stress loop, causing the repair to be rolled back even though the probability condition is now correct.
rules.guidance: For generated probabilistic membership tests, keep the false-positive assertion one-sided: `observed - expected > tolerance`. If that change makes the generated harness run until the timeout, reduce only the generated stress workload to a representative finite set or optimize the membership path, while keeping edge cases for zero or tiny capacity and at least a few requested probabilities. Do not weaken inserted-key membership assertions. A timeout after a negative probability difference is not evidence for restoring an absolute-value probability check.

rules.title: Replace local capacity defaults with the expected field value
rules.trigger: A parser/output wrapper has a local default capacity constant, and equality fails only on the returned capacity field.
rules.goal: Apply the visible capacity contract with the smallest compile-safe edit.
rules.constraint: Do not alter parsing control flow, entry storage, or getter behavior when only the capacity field differs.
rules.risk: A broad repair can introduce compile errors or regress parsing while leaving the single wrong default unchanged.
rules.guidance: When the failure shows `left: ... capacity: A` and `right: ... capacity: B`, inspect the returned wrapper constructor and any nearby local constant such as `DEFAULT_CAPACITY`, `INITIAL_CAPACITY`, or a literal assigned to `capacity`. The repair should be narrow: replace A with B in that semantic returned-capacity source, then ensure every successful return path uses it. Leave count, entries, error handling, and value parsing untouched unless they have a separate failing assertion. If a previous repair changed many parser branches and failed to compile, roll back to the narrow constant/field replacement.

rules.title: Read declaration names as the rest of the record
rules.trigger: Lookup fails for a declared public name that contains spaces, brackets, ranges, indexes, or other suffix text.
rules.goal: Store the full public declaration name while keeping the compact identifier token separate.
rules.constraint: Do not stop the visible name at the next whitespace byte after the base token.
rules.risk: The declaration table is populated under a shortened name, so public lookup fails even though the identifier and size were parsed.
rules.guidance: For declaration records with fields like type, size, identifier, and public name, parse the identifier as one token, then read the public name from the remaining record payload up to the terminator marker. Trim only outer whitespace and terminator text; preserve internal spaces and bracketed or ranged suffixes. Code that reads the name with a delimiter set containing plain space is a red flag: replace it with a bounded read until the declaration terminator, then remove the trailing terminator token before copying to the fixed-size public name buffer.

rules.title: Timestamp helpers share the outer file cursor
rules.trigger: A file parser reads a timestamp marker in the outer loop and then parses the timestamp in a helper.
rules.goal: Advance the same cursor that the assignment/declaration loop will read next.
rules.constraint: Do not clone or reopen the file in timestamp helpers, because the outer loop must observe the consumed digits.
rules.risk: The timestamp value can be parsed from a cloned handle, while the real parser cursor remains before the digits and later treats them as value assignments or garbage.
rules.guidance: When the outer loop consumes a marker and calls a timestamp helper, the helper must read digits from the same cursor object and stop at the same byte boundary as the C scanner. Avoid `try_clone`, fresh file opens, and buffered readers in that helper just as in directive and assignment helpers. If the handle is passed as a shared file reference, perform `Read` and `Seek` on that same reference; do not bind a new owned file from it.

rules.title: Negative false-positive difference is not a failure
rules.trigger: A generated probabilistic test prints `bad probability` with an observed-minus-expected difference that is negative.
rules.goal: Preserve one-sided false-positive bounds instead of rejecting a filter that is more selective than requested.
rules.constraint: Do not repair production membership logic solely because a generated test uses an absolute difference around the probability gap.
rules.risk: A correct or improved filter still fails because the generated harness treats lower false-positive rates as too far from the requested probability.
rules.guidance: If the diagnostic prints a negative value for `observed - expected`, fix the generated check rather than weakening the implementation. Replace two-sided checks such as `(observed - expected).abs() > tolerance`, `abs(observed - expected) > tolerance`, or equivalent absolute-value logic with the one-sided source condition `observed - expected > tolerance`. Keep inserted-key membership assertions unchanged. A negative printed difference is passing evidence for an upper-bound false-positive test.

rules.title: Use the expected capacity literal on every success path
rules.trigger: A returned struct equality failure shows matching entries and count, with only the public capacity field differing.
rules.goal: Make returned capacity a semantic output field instead of an allocation default.
rules.constraint: Do not keep a default such as 16, 32, or Vec capacity when the visible expected value is a different literal or named public constant.
rules.risk: A parser can be otherwise correct and still fail every empty, comment-only, or zero-entry success case because it returns the internal allocation size.
rules.guidance: When the diff exposes `left: ... capacity: A` and `right: ... capacity: B` while entries and count are identical, the right-side capacity is the public contract. Replace the internal default with that exact visible capacity for all successful returns from the same wrapper, including empty input, whitespace/comment-only input, and parsed non-empty input. Keep count tied to parsed entries, but keep capacity tied to the caller-visible fixture, constructor, interface default, or expected literal. Do not derive this field from Vec::capacity(), max token length, current entry count, or a convenient initial allocation.

rules.title: Shared file parsers must read from the same handle
rules.trigger: A text-format parser finds declarations or directives, but later lookups miss data because a helper read from a cloned or prefetched file cursor.
rules.goal: Keep all helper reads synchronized with the outer parser's current byte position.
rules.constraint: Do not call `try_clone`, reopen the path, wrap a fresh `BufReader`, or use any reader that can prefetch bytes from a shared file cursor.
rules.risk: The helper appears to parse one directive locally, but the outer loop resumes from a stale position and skips declarations, timestamps, or value assignments.
rules.guidance: For helpers called after the outer parser has consumed a marker or peeked a byte, pass and use the same mutable cursor object. If the handle type is shared-reference based, perform `Read` and `Seek` operations on that exact reference without cloning the OS file description. Read bounded payloads byte-by-byte or with a non-prefetching cursor wrapper, stop at the same delimiter as the source scanset, and leave the delimiter consumption exactly as the caller expects. A visible `try_clone`, new file open, or new buffered reader inside a directive/value helper is a repair target, not an implementation detail.

rules.title: Keep bracket suffixes in declaration names
rules.trigger: A parser reports that a declared signal or field cannot be found when the expected public name includes a bracketed range or suffix.
rules.goal: Preserve the complete visible declaration name, not only the first whitespace-delimited token.
rules.constraint: Do not parse declaration names with a fixed token index when the source scanset keeps text until a terminator marker.
rules.risk: The identifier table is populated, but public lookup fails because `name [N:M]` was stored as only `name`.
rules.guidance: After reading the declaration type, size, and identifier code, treat the remaining payload before the terminator as the public name field. Trim outer whitespace and the terminator marker, but preserve internal spaces and bracketed suffixes such as ranges, indexes, or packed dimensions. If a first pass split on whitespace, append any following bracketed token to the visible name with one separating space. Store that full visible name in the declaration record while keeping the compact identifier code separately for value assignments.

rules.title: Start table-backed filters in table mode before bloom upgrade
rules.trigger: A probabilistic membership structure reports a false-positive rate near one, or every uninserted key appears present after construction and insertion.
rules.goal: Preserve the source two-phase design: exact table first, bit-array filter only after the grow threshold chooses to upgrade.
rules.constraint: Do not allocate or activate the bit array in the constructor when the source constructor starts with no bit storage and no buckets.
rules.risk: Starting directly in bit mode with too few bytes makes most hash probes collide, so inserted-key checks pass while false positives explode.
rules.guidance: For a structure that begins as an exact open-addressed table and later upgrades to a probabilistic bit array, mirror the empty constructor state literally: count zero, no active buckets, and no bit storage. On the first insertion, run the same grow path the source would run; allocate table buckets or upgrade to bit storage only when that grow threshold says so. Compute the final bit universe as the same power-of-two value used by the source mask, derive byte length from that final bit count, and keep the hash count at least one. During upgrade, reinsert only real occupied table keys into the bit array, stripping any probe-distance or metadata bits before hashing. A `bad probability` failure with an observed rate close to one is evidence that the constructor or upgrade path activated an undersized bit array too early, not just a generated-test tolerance issue.

rules.title: Parse RGBA alpha separately from RGB bytes
rules.trigger: Formatted color output or parsed color equality differs only in the alpha byte, especially for an input alpha of `1` or `1.0`.
rules.goal: Preserve the C contract where RGB components are byte values but alpha is normalized to the range 0..1 before storage.
rules.constraint: Do not parse all four rgba components with the same byte parser.
rules.risk: A parser can accept the color and print the right shape, but `rgba(..., 1)` is stored as alpha byte 1 instead of 255.
rules.guidance: Parse RGB and alpha with different rules. The first three components must be integers in the byte range 0..255. The fourth component is normalized in the numeric range 0..1, whether written as an integer or a float. After validating the alpha range, multiply it by 255 before storing the public byte value. Thus alpha `0` stores `0`, `0.5` stores about `128` according to the source rounding/cast behavior, and `1` or `1.0` stores `255`. Do not reuse the RGB byte parser for alpha, and do not clamp invalid alpha values such as `1.5`; report the same parse error as C.

rules.title: Read value assignment lines from the shared cursor
rules.trigger: A directive/header parser finds declarations, but value lookup at a timestamp returns no value for a declared signal or field.
rules.goal: Keep assignment parsing synchronized with the outer file loop and store value changes on the declaration's identifier index.
rules.constraint: Do not use `try_clone`, a fresh buffered reader, or any reader that can prefetch from the same file handle and leave the outer cursor at a different position.
rules.risk: Declarations and metadata pass, but assignments are skipped or attached to the wrong signal because the shared cursor was desynchronized by a cloned buffered read.
rules.guidance: For line-oriented value changes after an outer loop has peeked or ungot the first byte, read the assignment from the same file handle byte-by-byte or with a cursor wrapper that does not prefetch beyond the line. Preserve the source scanset boundary: read until newline or EOF, parse the line, and leave or consume the newline exactly as the outer loop expects. For scalar assignments, split the first value byte from the following identifier. For vector assignments, split the value token and identifier token, strip only the syntax prefix such as leading `b` from the stored value, and use the identifier mapping to select the existing declaration slot. Append the timestamped value to that signal/field without creating a new declaration. A failure like `no value found at timestamp` after declaration lookup succeeds usually means the assignment helper did not store the change on the shared indexed object.

rules.title: Keep generated probability checks as upper bounds
rules.trigger: A probabilistic membership test reports `bad probability` even though the measured false-positive rate is lower than the requested probability.
rules.goal: Avoid rejecting a filter that is more selective than the requested false-positive rate.
rules.constraint: Do not use absolute difference when the source test only rejects rates that are too high.
rules.risk: The implementation inserts and finds all real keys, but a generated test fails because `(observed - expected).abs()` treats lower false-positive rates as bad.
rules.guidance: Compare the original C test before repairing the data structure. If the source condition is one-sided, such as `(observed - p) > tolerance && n > 0`, preserve that exact direction in generated Rust tests. Replace checks like `(observed - p).abs() > tolerance && n > 0` with `observed - p > tolerance && n > 0`. Keep the inserted-key membership assertions unchanged; only the false-positive tolerance should be one-sided. A negative printed difference is evidence that the filter is below the requested rate, not that the implementation is incorrect.

rules.title: Separate in-memory Display from stream line output
rules.trigger: Formatted object equality fails even though parsed fields and stream-oriented printer behavior are otherwise correct.
rules.goal: Match exact string output for both `to_string()` and file/stream printing.
rules.constraint: Do not implement an in-memory `Display` formatter by writing a newline after every entry when equality expects no final newline.
rules.risk: A printer translated from C line output needs newlines, but `to_string()` fails due to one synthetic trailing newline after the final record.
rules.guidance: Keep two formatting contracts separate. A stream helper translated from `fprintf(..., "\n")` should emit one newline per record. A `Display` implementation used by `to_string()` should emit separators between records and no separator after the final record unless the expected string explicitly includes it. Implement this by enumerating entries up to the public count, writing `\n` before entries after the first or after every entry except the last, then writing the entry body. Do not call the stream helper from `Display`, and do not call `Display` from the stream helper if their final-newline contracts differ. Preserve value spelling exactly: quoted strings, lowercase booleans, fixed six-decimal floats, and color bytes in the public order.

rules.title: Clamp tiny probabilistic filters before deriving storage
rules.trigger: A bloom-like or probabilistic set panics in bit insertion/check with a huge bit index, an empty bit universe, or `m == 0`.
rules.goal: Keep capacity, bit count, hash count, storage length, and mask arithmetic coherent for tiny inputs.
rules.constraint: Do not special-case a requested zero or tiny capacity into `m == 0` while later allocating one byte and indexing it with an unmasked hash.
rules.risk: The first insertion upgrades to bit mode with storage length one, but the bit mask is all ones because the derived bit universe is zero, so hash bits become an out-of-bounds byte index.
rules.guidance: Before computing derived bloom/filter metadata, apply the source minimum requested capacity. If the C constructor clamps requests below a minimum, do that first for zero and tiny requests too. Then compute the requested bit count, round the bit universe to the same power-of-two value used by C masks, and keep the hash count at least one. Allocate storage from the final nonzero bit universe, not by `max(1)` around an otherwise zero `m`. A valid invariant is: if bit storage is nonempty, then `m > 0`, `m` matches the mask `m - 1`, `k > 0`, and every bit index is `(hash & (m - 1))` before converting to byte index. Constructors that start in table mode should keep bit storage empty until upgrade; they should not preallocate table buckets from the bit count unless the C constructor does.

rules.title: Parse numeric prefixes without swallowing following units
rules.trigger: A directive or header parser fills the numeric scale/count field but leaves the adjacent unit/suffix field empty.
rules.goal: Preserve C scanf behavior where `%zu%[^...]` reads a digit prefix and then starts the following scanset at the first non-digit byte.
rules.constraint: Do not read a numeric field until whitespace when the source format allows the unit text to immediately follow the digits.
rules.risk: Inputs like `1s`, `10ms`, or `64kb` are parsed as one failed integer token or as a number with an empty unit.
rules.guidance: When translating adjacent scanf directives such as `%zu%[^$\n]`, parse the unsigned number from consecutive ASCII digits only. Stop at the first non-digit and leave that byte for the following field. Then read the suffix/unit scanset until the delimiter used by the C format, trimming only the API-invisible surrounding whitespace or terminator text that the source ignores. Do not require whitespace between the number and unit unless the C format has whitespace there. This applies inside shared-cursor directive parsers too: after the numeric prefix, continue from the same cursor position to fill the unit buffer.

rules.title: Visible returned capacity beats internal defaults
rules.trigger: A returned parser/output struct compares equal on entries and count, but only the public capacity field differs.
rules.goal: Preserve capacity as caller-visible state, not as a private allocation guess.
rules.constraint: Do not hardcode a convenient internal default when the wrapper has no capacity argument and visible expected output shows another capacity.
rules.risk: Empty, whitespace-only, comment-only, or successfully parsed inputs can all fail equality even though their entries are correct.
rules.guidance: When a C API fills caller-owned storage and the Rust API returns a struct by value, the returned capacity field represents the caller-visible storage contract. If an equality diff, fixture constructor, public helper constant, or interface setup shows the expected capacity, reuse that value for every successful parse/load return. Keep count equal to the number of parsed entries, but do not derive capacity from count, Vec allocation, token buffer sizes, maximum key/value constants, or a fallback chosen only for the Rust implementation. A left/right diff where entries and count match but capacity differs is a direct signal to replace the internal default with the visible contract value.

rules.title: Do not accept runtime-reachable placeholder bodies
rules.trigger: Compilation succeeds but a runtime check panics at `not implemented`, `unimplemented!`, `todo!`, or a placeholder panic.
rules.goal: Finish the callable body from the original C behavior before treating the translation or repair as successful.
rules.constraint: Do not let compile repair replace a difficult helper with a stub just because type checking then passes.
rules.risk: The project looks translated in per-callable logs, but the first integrated run panics immediately in a reachable helper.
rules.guidance: After any compile repair, scan the changed callable and directly reachable helpers for `unimplemented!()`, `todo!()`, placeholder `panic!`, dummy constant returns, or comments that say the body is omitted. If the panic location points at such a helper, repair the helper itself instead of changing the caller or generated harness. Use the original C body as the source of truth and translate the smallest direct behavior: unsigned wrapping arithmetic for bit/hash helpers, shared-cursor reads for parser helpers, and the same return/error convention as the C function. A callable that still contains a reachable placeholder must be considered failed even if `cargo check` passed.

rules.title: Complete shared-cursor instruction parser helpers
rules.trigger: A file parser helper called after a directive marker is left as a placeholder or desynchronizes the outer file cursor.
rules.goal: Translate the directive helper as a complete shared-cursor state machine.
rules.constraint: Do not create a fresh buffered reader that prefetches from the same file, and do not leave directive branches as placeholders.
rules.risk: The outer loop has already consumed a marker byte, then the helper panics or consumes too much input, so later declarations, timestamps, or assignments are never seen correctly.
rules.guidance: For directive-oriented text formats, the outer loop often consumes a marker such as `$` or `#` and then calls a helper on the same file handle. The helper must read from that same cursor, parse the next instruction token, update parser state, and skip only the bytes the C scansets consume. Implement all common directive branches instead of stubbing them: end/dump directives return success; scope/upscope/comment/end-definition style directives skip payload up to but not including the next marker when the source scanset preserves it; variable/declaration directives fill the public signal/field record and identifier index; date/version/timescale style directives copy payload text until the delimiter. If a branch is intentionally ignored, it should still consume exactly the source branch's payload and return the same success value.

rules.title: Translate unsigned hash mix helpers as wrapping avalanche code
rules.trigger: A hash-table, bloom-like, or probabilistic membership structure calls a mix/helper function that remains a placeholder.
rules.goal: Keep the add/check key path deterministic and identical to the C unsigned arithmetic.
rules.constraint: Do not replace a C bit-mixing helper with a stub, ordinary non-wrapping arithmetic, a random hash, or a constant.
rules.risk: All table growth and membership logic depends on the mixed key; a placeholder panics, while a different mix can make inserted keys disappear or change false-positive behavior.
rules.guidance: For a small unsigned mix helper, translate the C sequence literally with Rust wrapping operations. Preserve xor-shift order, constants, and word width. For SplitMix-style finalizers this usually means `key ^= key >> 30`, `key = key.wrapping_mul(0xbf58476d1ce4e5b9)`, `key ^= key >> 27`, `key = key.wrapping_mul(0x94d049bb133111eb)`, `key ^= key >> 31`, then return key. Use `wrapping_mul` for every C unsigned multiply, keep shifts below the word width, and mask packed-key payload bits only where the C macros do so. Do not use the standard library hasher for this path because add and check must reproduce the same low-level key stream.

rules.title: Keep Display strings free of synthetic trailing newlines
rules.trigger: Tests compare `to_string()` or formatted output exactly after parser and getter behavior already passes.
rules.goal: Match exact in-memory display strings while preserving stream-printer newline behavior separately.
rules.constraint: Do not implement `Display` by blindly calling `writeln!` for every entry when the expected string has no trailing newline.
rules.risk: All parsed values can be correct while `to_string()` fails because it appends one extra newline after the last record.
rules.guidance: Separate formatting contracts. A stream printer translated from `fprintf(..., "\n")` should write a newline after each emitted entry. A `Display` implementation used by `to_string()` should usually write separators between entries: write a newline before entries after the first, or after every entry except the last, and do not add a final newline unless the expected string includes it. Keep value formatting unchanged: strings quoted, floats with six decimals, booleans lowercase, and colors formatted as `rgba(r, g, b, a)`.

rules.title: Preserve bracket suffixes in declaration names
rules.trigger: A declaration parser stores a signal or field name and lookups fail for names that include a bracketed range suffix.
rules.goal: Keep the lookup-visible name equal to the test/API-visible declaration name.
rules.constraint: Do not stop the stored name at the base identifier if the surrounding declaration syntax treats a following bracket range as part of the visible name.
rules.risk: The parser can load the file and store signal sizes, but `get_by_name("name [n:0]")` fails because only `name` was stored.
rules.guidance: When parsing declarations like `$var ... <id> <name> [range] $end` or similar token streams, read the base name and then inspect following tokens before the declaration terminator. If the next token is a bracketed range, append it to the stored visible name with the same separating space the tests/API use. Continue to stop before the declaration terminator and do not consume the terminator if the outer cursor expects it. Keep aliases and id indexing separate from the visible name: the identifier maps the storage slot, while the full name is what lookup compares.

rules.title: Keep generated false-positive checks one-sided
rules.trigger: A probabilistic set or bloom-filter generated test reports `bad probability` when measured false positives are lower than the requested rate.
rules.goal: Avoid rejecting a correct or better-than-requested false-positive rate.
rules.constraint: Do not use absolute error when the C test only rejects rates that exceed the requested probability by too much.
rules.risk: A valid implementation fails only because `abs(observed - expected)` treats a lower false-positive rate as bad.
rules.guidance: For translated tests around probabilistic filters, compare the source test condition before changing the data structure. If C checks `(observed - p) > tolerance && n > 0`, preserve that one-sided condition. A generated Rust check like `(observed - p).abs() > tolerance && n > 0` is too strict because it rejects lower false-positive rates. Repair the generated test condition to `observed - p > tolerance && n > 0`; do not weaken membership assertions for inserted keys.

rules.title: Treat block ECC check bytes as sidecar metadata
rules.trigger: A block error-correcting codec copies data bytes unchanged and appends one check byte per fixed-size block.
rules.goal: Match the source check-byte arithmetic without reinterpreting the block as an interleaved full codeword.
rules.constraint: Do not pack the data bytes and check byte into one synthetic integer with parity slots inserted between data bits when the C encoder emits the original data bytes verbatim followed by a sidecar check byte.
rules.risk: The encoder can produce the expected sidecar byte, but the decoder rejects clean data or flips the wrong bit because it recomputes parity over parity-bit positions that were never stored in the data stream.
rules.guidance: When the encoded layout is `data bytes + check byte`, leave the data bytes in place. Walk only the data bits in byte/bit order, map each data bit to the same logical Hamming position used by C, and skip parity positions in that logical counter. Encode the low syndrome as the xor of positions for set data bits, then set the high overall-parity bit from the parity of all data bytes and the low syndrome bits. Decode by copying the data bytes out first, recomputing the low syndrome from those copied bytes, xoring with `check & 0x7f`, and recomputing overall parity from data bytes plus the received check byte. A zero syndrome accepts the block. A nonzero syndrome with even overall parity rejects as a double error. A nonzero power-of-two syndrome means only a parity bit changed, so accept without changing data. A non-power-of-two syndrome maps back to a data-bit index by subtracting the count of skipped parity positions below it, then flips that data bit if it lies inside the received data length.

rules.title: Preserve config alpha scaling and stable open errors
rules.trigger: A config parser/printer fails on rgba alpha output or file-open diagnostics after other key/value tests pass.
rules.goal: Keep the C parser's printed values and public error strings byte-for-byte stable.
rules.constraint: Do not parse the alpha component like an RGB byte, and do not expose host OS error text when the C API reports a fixed open-failure message.
rules.risk: The parser accepts all entries but prints `rgba(..., 1)` instead of `rgba(..., 255)`, or returns `No such file or directory` instead of the expected API error text.
rules.guidance: For `rgba(r, g, b, a)`, RGB components are integers in `[0,255]`, but alpha is normalized in `[0,1]` whether written as an integer or float; multiply alpha by 255 before storing the byte. Match the C cast/rounding expectation shown by tests, and print colors as `rgba(r, g, b, a)` with the stored byte values. For load-from-file wrappers, validate filename and extension first, then map any failed open/read of an otherwise valid config path to the API's stable message such as `failed to open file` rather than forwarding platform-specific IO text. Keep `Display` and explicit print helpers on the same formatting contract: strings quoted, floats with six decimals, booleans lowercase, one newline after each entry when writing to a stream.

rules.title: Do not consume scanf scanset delimiters
rules.trigger: A translated parser emulates C fscanf scansets such as `%[^$]`, `%[^\n]`, or skip scansets and then the outer loop reports an unexpected character.
rules.goal: Preserve the source cursor position around delimiter-driven parsing.
rules.constraint: Do not read past and discard the delimiter when the C scanset would stop before it.
rules.risk: The parser handles the first instruction or field but then sees bare text such as an `end` token without its marker, or rejects a valid file with an unexpected-character error.
rules.guidance: C scansets like `%[^$]` and `%*[^$]` consume characters only up to but not including the delimiter; the following outer `fgetc` or parser step must still see that delimiter. When translating to Rust byte reads, stop before consuming the delimiter by peeking, seeking back one byte, or using a buffered cursor that can leave the delimiter unread. Apply the same rule to newline scansets if a later parser expects the newline. If the parser receives a shared file handle, every helper must advance the same underlying cursor in the same order as C; avoid making a fresh buffered reader that prefetches bytes and leaves the outer file offset inconsistent.

rules.title: Initialize derived bloom metadata before membership operations
rules.trigger: A bloom-like public struct can be constructed with count/probability fields but zero derived bit count, hash count, word count, or backing storage.
rules.goal: Make add/check/fingerprint paths use a coherent derived bit universe even when callers bypass the preferred constructor.
rules.constraint: Do not let zero derived metadata turn membership checks into vacuous success or modulo-by-zero panics.
rules.risk: Generated or hand-written tests may build the public struct directly; fingerprint panics on `% 0`, add never records data because the hash-count is zero, and check returns true for every key because there are no hashes to test.
rules.guidance: Before fingerprint, add, check, join, or write operations, ensure derived fields are initialized from the public capacity/probability contract. If the bit count, hash count, word count, or bit array is zero but the public capacity/probability are valid, compute the same values as the constructor, allocate the backing bit words/bytes, and store the derived metadata. If the operation only has an immutable receiver, compute local derived values for fingerprint/check and treat missing storage as an empty filter rather than a universal match. A zero-hash loop should never make `check` return true for arbitrary input; missing or empty storage means definitely not present unless the source explicitly documents otherwise.
keywords: remainder with a divisor of zero

rules.title: Keep power-of-two Robin Hood bloom growth semantics
rules.trigger: A dynamic bloom filter starts as a Robin Hood hash table, upgrades to a bit array, or times out during the first add/grow cycle.
rules.goal: Preserve the constructor, growth threshold, packed bucket layout, and upgrade transition exactly enough to avoid zero-sized loops.
rules.constraint: Do not allow small requested capacities to produce `m == 0`, `k == 0`, or a zero-length upgraded bit array; do not preallocate a table if the C constructor starts empty and relies on the first add to grow.
rules.risk: The first insertion can spin forever because growth upgrades to an empty bit vector, or lookups fail because packed displacement bits are mixed into the key during reinsert/upgrade.
rules.guidance: For Robin-Hood-to-bloom designs, clamp tiny requested capacities to the source minimum before computing bits. Round the bit universe up to a power of two when the source masks with `m - 1`, and keep the hash count at least one. If the C constructor leaves bucket storage null with `nbuckets == 0`, do the same and let the first add call grow. In grow, compute the new bucket count first; if the table should upgrade, allocate `m >> 3` bytes only after `m` is nonzero and power-of-two, clear table storage, and reinsert old occupied buckets through the bloom path using only the low key bits, not the top displacement byte. In table mode, preserve the top-byte displacement and low-key packing for insert, lookup, swaps, and reinsertion. Add a bounded full-table scan or a growth fallback rather than an unbounded probe loop.

rules.title: Infer returned wrapper capacity from the visible contract
rules.trigger: A parser or loader returns a struct with entries/count/capacity, but the Rust wrapper has no capacity argument.
rules.goal: Preserve the caller-visible default capacity independently from parsed entry count or internal maximum token sizes.
rules.constraint: Do not use an unrelated C buffer-size macro or Vec allocation capacity as the returned semantic capacity field.
rules.risk: The parser can accept all entries but fail equality on empty or comment-only inputs because capacity is set to an internal maximum instead of the wrapper default.
rules.guidance: When a C API fills caller-owned output storage but the Rust wrapper returns the output struct by value, treat capacity as part of the public contract. If tests, interface code, constructors, or helper constants show a default capacity, use that value for every successful return, including empty input and zero-entry special cases. Keep count equal to parsed entries. Do not derive capacity from entries.len(), Vec::capacity(), key/value buffer limits, or maximum token constants unless those are the actual public constructor capacity.

rules.title: Allocate bloom bit arrays before setting indexed bits
rules.trigger: A bloom-like filter computes bit indexes from hash positions, but check/write paths panic because the bit array is empty or shorter than the declared bit count.
rules.goal: Keep the declared filter size, number of hash functions, storage length, and bit-indexing convention consistent.
rules.constraint: Do not update filter metadata or headers without allocating the backing bit array that membership operations index.
rules.risk: Header parsing and formatted output can pass while membership checks or writes panic with an index into a zero-length bit vector.
rules.guidance: After computing the bit count, allocate enough bytes or words for every possible bit index before any add, check, write, or readback path runs. Convert a bit index into byte/word index and mask using the same endian convention as the C code, and bounds-check against the allocated storage length. When reading a serialized filter, resize the bit storage from the serialized bit count before copying payload bits. Empty filters still need storage sized to the declared bit universe if later checks index into it.

rules.title: Preserve SECDED check-byte parity and bit positions
rules.trigger: A single-error-correcting code appends or consumes a check byte and roundtrip or one-bit repair tests disagree by one parity byte or reject correctable data.
rules.goal: Match the C check-byte construction and correction arithmetic exactly.
rules.constraint: Do not treat the high parity bit as independent from the low syndrome before reproducing the source arithmetic.
rules.risk: Encoding can be off by one check bit, and decoding can reject a single data-bit error because parity was recomputed from only part of the check byte.
rules.guidance: Walk data bits in the same code-position order as C, skipping power-of-two parity positions. Accumulate the low syndrome from set data bits and accumulate the overall parity from every data byte. Before appending the check byte, fold the parity of the low syndrome into the high parity bit. During decode, xor the recomputed low syndrome with the low seven bits of the received check byte. If the syndrome is zero, accept. Otherwise recompute the overall parity using the whole received check byte before deciding whether the error is correctable. For a non-power-of-two syndrome, map the code position back to the data-bit index by subtracting the number of parity positions below it.

rules.title: Grow sparse dictionaries before probe space is exhausted
rules.trigger: A sparse or open-addressed dictionary accepts early inserts but returns failure once probe count reaches the current occupied count or load threshold.
rules.goal: Keep insert, lookup, resize, and bucket_count semantics consistent for long insertion sequences.
rules.constraint: Do not stop probing only because the number of probes exceeded the current live count when empty slots may exist after collisions.
rules.risk: Small set/get tests pass, but repeated insertions fail at a low iteration because the table never grows or because the probe bound is tied to live count rather than capacity.
rules.guidance: Compute the hash with C unsigned wrapping arithmetic, probe within the bucket capacity, and stop only after a full bounded scan or after finding an empty slot/matching key. When load factor crosses the source threshold, allocate a larger bucket array, reset the live count, and reinsert every occupied entry through the same insertion path without duplicating or freeing payloads prematurely. Keep bucket_count as the number of occupied entries, not the maximum probe count, and keep bucket_max as allocated capacity.

rules.title: Report missing config values after a consumed delimiter
rules.trigger: A colon-delimited config parser reports a separator error after it already consumed the separator.
rules.goal: Keep parser diagnostics tied to grammar position: missing separator before the delimiter, missing value after it.
rules.constraint: Do not return a separator-missing diagnostic once the delimiter was consumed.
rules.risk: A parser can accept most entries but misclassify `key:` as a delimiter problem instead of a value problem.
rules.guidance: Split entry parsing into key scanning, delimiter consumption, whitespace skipping, then value parsing. If the delimiter is absent, return the original separator diagnostic. If the delimiter was consumed and the next visible token is newline, comment, or end-of-input, return the missing-value diagnostic. Keep invalid first-key characters and invalid value characters on their existing error paths.

rules.title: Build generated byte views without undeclared crates
rules.trigger: A generated Rust test or helper references a byte-view crate that is not declared by the crate under test.
rules.goal: Keep generated tests compileable while preserving the native byte order passed by the C test.
rules.constraint: Do not add a new dependency or edit Cargo.toml only to satisfy generated test scaffolding.
rules.risk: The translated library can be correct while test compilation fails before exercising it because the generated helper imports an undeclared crate.
rules.guidance: Replace unavailable byte-view helpers with local conversions: use integer `to_ne_bytes()` for scalar keys, concatenate field bytes explicitly for plain structs, and keep the same native-endian field order used by the C caller. Prefer a small helper in the generated test module over changing production dependencies.

rules.title: Create relative roundtrip fixtures before reading them
rules.trigger: A generated read or join test fails with a missing file before it observes production behavior.
rules.goal: Make readback tests set up their own project-local files and then reopen those files through the public API.
rules.constraint: Do not hard-code absolute source paths, skip read assertions, or assume repository fixture files exist in the output crate.
rules.risk: A correct serializer or reader can still look broken because the generated test opens a fixture that was never created in the test sandbox.
rules.guidance: Before any readback, create the needed file relative to the current test crate, create parent directories if needed, remove or truncate stale files, write through the public writer or the same binary layout expected by the reader, flush or close the handle, then reopen through the public read or join API. Keep all paths relative to the current working directory.

rules.title: Skip out-of-universe members during generated intersections
rules.trigger: A set or range intersection setup unwraps a range error for an input member outside the declared universe.
rules.goal: Let generated intersection checks match C behavior by treating impossible members as absent from that operation.
rules.constraint: Do not turn explicit range-validation APIs into silent success; narrow the tolerance to constructor or filtering paths used to build derived intersections.
rules.risk: Most set operations can pass while one derived intersection fails early because setup rejects a member that the C path would ignore.
rules.guidance: For intersection setup, filter, or derived-set construction, skip members outside the support/universe before returning the result. Preserve the public out-of-range error for APIs whose purpose is direct validation or insertion. The derived set should contain only in-universe members and should not panic or return an error just because one source candidate is outside the universe.

rules.title: Preserve two-lane bit-interleave contracts
rules.trigger: A two-lane bit-spreading encoder or decoder returns a transposed lane, bit-reversed code, or single decoded coordinate for a paired-coordinate value.
rules.goal: Match the C spread-bits sequence, final lane combine order, and paired-coordinate decode contract exactly.
rules.constraint: Do not swap coordinate lanes, reverse bit numbering, or collapse a public two-coordinate decode into a single-lane helper result.
rules.risk: A plausible interleave implementation can compile and pass simple zero cases while returning the transposed code, or a generated harness can compare one decoded lane against both original coordinates.
rules.guidance: Translate the C spread-bits helper literally: mask and shift each coordinate with the same constants and width, including leading-zero C octal shift counts such as 020 and 010. Keep the even-lane source and odd-lane source from the C code, then combine the expanded lanes in the same even/odd position order. If a failure is exactly transposed, swap only the final lane combine order; do not rewrite the whole spreading algorithm or reverse all bits. When generated Rust exposes only a single-lane deinterleave helper but the C public API decodes a pair, decode both lanes explicitly by calling the helper on the unshifted code and on the one-bit-shifted code, then compare or assign each result to the matching original coordinate.

rules.title: Set bitmap membership before updating counts
rules.trigger: A bitmap container reports the right cardinality after fill/add but contains() returns false for a filled member.
rules.goal: Keep membership bits or values and cardinality metadata synchronized.
rules.constraint: Do not update cardinality, container keys, or range metadata without also setting every observable member.
rules.risk: Range inserts can appear successful by count alone while membership queries fail because the data container was not populated.
rules.guidance: When inserting or filling a range, first write every member into the array or bit-vector representation, then update cardinality from the actual members. During array-to-bit-vector conversion, copy all existing values into the bit-vector before switching representation. Keep container keys sorted and avoid metadata-only fast paths unless contains() observes the same range.

rules.title: Treat C string offsets as byte indexes
rules.trigger: A translated substring, string length, or encoding conversion path uses Unicode scalar indexes where C used byte offsets.
rules.goal: Preserve byte-oriented slicing and deterministic code-unit conversion while staying within Rust bounds.
rules.constraint: Do not use Rust character positions unless the C helper explicitly counts code points.
rules.risk: Rust string APIs can silently change byte-oriented C behavior, causing shorter slices, boundary panics, or different encoded code units.
rules.guidance: Keep public offsets and lengths as byte offsets. Operate on `&[u8]` for slicing, clamp start/length to the byte buffer, and convert back to the interface type only after bounds are settled. For encoding conversion, map the original byte or code-unit arrays literally instead of substituting similar characters or scalar-count lengths.

rules.title: Validate UTF-8 byte boundaries before slicing
rules.trigger: A UTF-8 helper panics on char boundaries or mishandles surrogate, overlong, invalid, or lossy conversion cases.
rules.goal: Return the interface's validation result instead of panicking on invalid byte ranges or invalid sequences.
rules.constraint: Do not index `str` with unchecked byte ranges; validate byte offsets and sequence legality first.
rules.risk: C-style validation APIs should report errors, but direct Rust slicing can panic before the API returns.
rules.guidance: Validate on bytes first. Check start/end are in range and on UTF-8 character boundaries before slicing; reject surrogate code points and overlong encodings explicitly; and make lossy conversion count replacement spans according to invalid byte runs. Return the crate's error or empty result for invalid boundaries rather than panicking.

rules.title: Recompute order-statistic counts after removal
rules.trigger: A tree removal keeps search mostly working but rank/select or manual node counts disagree after deleting a node.
rules.goal: Keep child counts, parent links, depth, and traversal count consistent after detach, replacement, and rotations.
rules.constraint: Do not only decrement ancestors of the removed node when a successor or predecessor is moved from another subtree.
rules.risk: Insertion and lookup can pass while deletion leaves stale left/right subtree counts and later order-statistic queries disagree with traversal.
rules.guidance: For deletion, detach the replacement candidate from its old parent, reconnect any lost child, move the candidate into the removed node's place, and update both subtrees' parent links. After every detach, rotation, and replacement, recompute left/right child counts from actual subtree sizes or run a fixup along all affected paths to root. The final count should equal an in-order traversal.

rules.title: Use available crypto backends instead of failure stubs
rules.trigger: A translated crypto wrapper compiles but key generation, blind/sign/finalize, verify, import, or export immediately returns a failure code.
rules.goal: Make the public wrapper perform the real operation through already-declared crypto dependencies.
rules.constraint: Do not leave reachable helpers returning a constant failure code when the crate already declares a suitable backend.
rules.risk: Structurally correct wrappers can make every test fail because all core operations are stubs.
rules.guidance: Inspect Cargo.toml and existing imports for crypto crates or FFI bindings, then implement the wrapper around those available APIs. Generate keys, serialize public/private material, perform the blind/sign/finalize or encrypt/decrypt step with the padding used by C, and verify through the matching backend call. If raw pointer access is difficult, prefer the high-level crate API over returning a failure stub.

rules.title: Preserve serialized string-key slot layout
rules.trigger: A deserializer rejects a valid string-key snapshot with a key type or key size conflict.
rules.goal: Round-trip string-key dictionaries with the same fixed slot and external bytes layout as the C serializer.
rules.constraint: Do not compare serialized string-key slots against one byte or the current string length when C stores a pointer-sized handle slot.
rules.risk: Ordinary key/value operations can pass while deserialization rejects valid snapshots because the fixed key slot size was recomputed differently from serialization.
rules.guidance: Use the same key-size calculation in deserialize that allocation and serialization used. For string keys, read the fixed pointer-sized or handle-sized slot, then reconstruct the actual string bytes from the serialized payload area before insertion. Validate headers against serialized slot sizes, not against the length of one reconstructed string.

rules.title: Mirror Motorola signal local-byte copy order
rules.trigger: A CAN/DBC Motorola signal roundtrip works for small integers but fails for wider signed or floating values.
rules.goal: Copy frame bytes into the local integer in the exact byte order used by the C helpers.
rules.constraint: Do not model Motorola order as a bit-reversed integer or rewrite the selected frame bytes in natural ascending order.
rules.risk: Bit indexes can look correct for short cases while a wider negative or floating value fails because the byte copy direction is off by one reversal.
rules.guidance: Keep index computation identical to C. For Motorola decode, copy from the least-significant frame byte down toward the most-significant frame byte into successive little-endian bytes of the local value. For encode, copy successive local little-endian bytes back into the frame in that same descending frame-byte order. Preserve sign extension and scaling after the local bytes are assembled.

rules.title: Keep non-empty linked collections circular
rules.trigger: An iterator over a linked collection panics because a next or previous link is absent before traversal wraps to the head.
rules.goal: Match C collection invariants where non-empty lists form a closed ring and iteration stops only on wraparound.
rules.constraint: Do not model the collection as null-terminated when append, remove, and iterate expect circular prev/next links.
rules.risk: Parsing or insertion can pass but iteration fails because tail.next or head.prev was never closed.
rules.guidance: On first insert, set prev and next to the node itself. On insert-before, insert-after, append, and remove, update all four adjacent links and keep the ring closed. Iteration should start at head, advance to next, and return None only when it wraps back to head. In safe Rust, emulate the ring with stable indices or arena storage instead of unwrapping nullable links.

rules.title: Use one open-address probe and equality invariant
rules.trigger: An open-addressed set fails add/remove/contains or set algebra after add and lookup used different probe or equality rules.
rules.goal: Make size, membership, deletion, and derived set operations agree on one stored-bucket invariant.
rules.constraint: Do not mix one probing formula in add with another in contains or remove. Do not leave remove as a stub.
rules.risk: Values can be inserted into buckets that later lookup never probes, or removal can break the probe cluster and make following members unreachable.
rules.guidance: Define one bucket-state convention, such as negative probe marker for empty/deleted and nonnegative marker for occupied. Use the same hash/index/probe walk and the same custom-or-byte equality helper for add, contains, and remove. Removal should clear the matching bucket, decrement size once, then repair the probe cluster with backward-shift deletion or by rebuilding occupied entries into fresh empty buckets. Union, intersection, difference, and disjoint checks should iterate occupied buckets and call the same membership helper.

rules.title: Drive public key traversal from one sorted store
rules.trigger: Tree or map traversal APIs compare forall, first/next, last/prev, prefix, ceil, or floor results against sorted unique keys.
rules.goal: Make every public traversal and lookup observe the same lexicographically sorted unique key set.
rules.constraint: Do not split state between a newly added sorted store and older traversal roots without updating every mutator.
rules.risk: A compatibility map can fix lookup but still fail traversal if insertion forgets vacant keys or forall walks stale structure.
rules.guidance: For public traversal contracts, keep one authoritative sorted key store. Initialize it in constructors, clear it in clear/reset, insert or update it in every put/set path, delete from it in removal, and derive size/empty/get/first/last/next/prev/prefix/ceil/floor/forall from that same store. Duplicates should update data without increasing count.

rules.title: Read one assignment line from the shared cursor
rules.trigger: A timestamped value-change parser loses later assignments after wrapping a shared file cursor in a buffered reader.
rules.goal: Consume exactly the current assignment line and leave the outer parser cursor at the next line.
rules.constraint: Do not create a buffered reader around a cloned shared file handle inside a one-line parser if read-ahead can advance the underlying cursor.
rules.risk: A parser can find declarations and timestamps but later value lookup returns none because read-ahead skipped assignment lines.
rules.guidance: Read bytes directly from the passed cursor until newline or EOF. Parse vector assignments into payload bits plus signal id, parse scalar assignments into scalar payload plus signal id, append one value change at the current timestamp, and return with the cursor positioned immediately after that line. Keep the current timestamp unchanged across consecutive assignment lines until the next timestamp marker.

rules.title: Preserve multi-token declaration names
rules.trigger: A declaration line has type, size, id, a visible name containing spaces or bracket suffixes, and an end marker.
rules.goal: Store the full public name from all name tokens after the id and before the end marker.
rules.constraint: Do not keep only the first name token after splitting a declaration by whitespace.
rules.risk: Lookup by the full visible name fails even though the parser read the declaration line.
rules.guidance: Parse declaration fields as type, size, id, then join every remaining token before the end marker with single spaces to form the public name. Store the full name, keep the id-to-signal mapping stable, resize signal arrays with empty entries if needed, and do not overwrite an existing first declaration unless the C state machine does.

rules.title: Split gap buffers by live text, not capacity bytes
rules.trigger: A gap-buffer split, backspace, move-gap, or get-string path exposes stale tail bytes from the backing capacity.
rules.goal: Keep gap location, gap length, visible length, and live tail slices consistent after mutations.
rules.constraint: Do not copy or print the whole backing capacity as visible text.
rules.risk: Insertion can pass while split or backspace returns a prefix plus stale bytes that should be hidden behind the gap.
rules.guidance: Compute visible text as prefix before the gap plus suffix after `gap_start + gap_len`, bounded by visible length. Split should copy only the logical suffix after the cursor into the new buffer, put the new buffer's gap at its start, and shrink the original visible length to the left side. Backspace should decrease gap position and visible length while increasing gap length without exposing removed bytes.

rules.title: Preserve parser and collection state together
rules.trigger: Parser cursors, token streams, lambda environments, hash buckets, set membership, or sparse table semantics are repaired together.
rules.goal: Keep state shared across helper calls without turning absent keys, empty buckets, or environments into local-only approximations.
rules.constraint: Do not reset parser cursors, hash buckets, set membership, or environments inside helpers that C keeps shared for the public operation.
rules.risk: A broad repair can improve one parser or collection case while regressing another by applying the wrong shortcut outside its state model.
rules.guidance: Use C helpers to identify the state carrier for each domain: parser cursor/token arrays, environment or definition tables, bucket occupancy, key equality, and deleted/empty sentinels. Preserve absent-key behavior explicitly rather than treating default values as present entries.

rules.title: Close parser entrypoints over reachable local helpers
rules.trigger: A public parser entrypoint sees private parse helpers, parser context methods, or recursive-descent stages that are still stubs.
rules.goal: Make the public parse call run complete parser logic without reaching unfinished module-level helpers.
rules.constraint: Do not implement an entrypoint as only context construction plus a call to a bare parse helper when that helper or its context methods are still unimplemented in the displayed shared items.
rules.risk: The crate can compile and the entrypoint body can look tidy, but runtime tests panic immediately when execution reaches a dangling parser helper.
rules.guidance: If the listed parse_regex/parse_term/parse_factor/parse_atom-style helpers or ParseContext methods are stubs, keep the full recursive-descent helper chain inside the public entrypoint as nested local functions over one shared cursor, or patch the helper impl only when that shared item is explicitly repairable. The entrypoint should consume the same cursor, construct AST/NFA/state objects locally, return parser errors instead of panicking, and check end-of-input after the local parse completes.

rules.title: Complete automaton minimization remap loops
rules.trigger: A deterministic automaton builder merges equivalent states, rebuilds a compact state list, or recomputes transition targets after minimization.
rules.goal: Return a fully remapped automaton with complete transition and terminal-state logic.
rules.constraint: Do not leave placeholder local variables, partially written loops, or a first pass that reads remapped indexes before every survivor and representative has a stable new index.
rules.risk: The translation can build most of the automaton correctly but fail compilation or tests at the final minimization step because merged transitions still point at old indexes or an unfinished self-index loop remains.
rules.guidance: When merging equivalent states, first compute each old state's representative, then assign new indexes to all surviving representatives, and only then build the compact state vector. Fill every transition through the representative-to-new-index map. Set per-state terminal or self-loop flags with an enumerate loop over the final vector, not with a placeholder self-index variable or a separate unfinished pass.

rules.title: Iterate byte alphabets without overflowing u8 endpoints
rules.trigger: A parser, regex engine, automaton, DFA/NFA serializer, or symbol-set formatter iterates over all byte values or rebuilds transitions for every character.
rules.goal: Cover exactly byte values 0 through 255 while keeping transition indexes valid after serialization and deserialization.
rules.constraint: Do not write an exclusive Rust range with an out-of-range u8 endpoint such as 0..256u8, and do not let missing transitions serialize as usize::MAX unless the reader explicitly maps that sentinel.
rules.risk: A repair can fix automaton logic conceptually but fail compilation on an overflowing u8 literal, or it can compile and then deserialize usize::MAX as an invalid target state.
rules.guidance: When the C code loops over the full unsigned char alphabet, use 0u16..=255 and cast inside the loop, or use 0..=u8::MAX. For transition tables, choose one sentinel convention for absent targets and use it symmetrically in serialize and deserialize; if the Rust reader validates target < states.len(), map absent targets to None before validation instead of decoding -1 as usize::MAX. When remapping minimized states, fill every byte transition through the representative/new-index map before writing the serialized table.

rules.title: Index NFA wrapper states in the vector that owns them
rules.trigger: A regex parser or automaton builder wraps an existing NFA for star, plus, optional, concatenation, alternation, padding, or complement operations.
rules.goal: Keep epsilon targets valid while adding synthetic start/final states around an existing state vector.
rules.constraint: Do not index the original pre-wrapper state vector with indexes that already include a prepended synthetic start offset. Do not leave epsilon targets pointing past states.len().
rules.risk: The parser can build simple NFAs but panic on repeat operators because old_final + 1 is used before the shifted states have been inserted into the new vector.
rules.guidance: Choose one indexing frame for each wrapper operation. If mutating the original vector before inserting a new start state, use original indexes such as old_final = nfa.final_ and write nfa.states[old_final].epsilon*. If building a new vector that starts with a synthetic state and then shifted old states, use shifted indexes only after the new vector exists, for example states[old_final + 1].epsilon*. Set the new final index to 1 + old_len only after accounting for the prepended start. After star/plus/optional/union/concat construction, every target, epsilon0, epsilon1, initial, and final index must be strictly less than states.len().

rules.title: Complete DFA decompilation with state elimination
rules.trigger: A regex or automaton public decompile/uncompile path is still a stub, or repairs mention local arrow/precedence helpers while converting a DFA back to a pattern.
rules.goal: Return a parseable regular expression for the DFA instead of leaving the decompile path as a placeholder.
rules.constraint: Do not leave `unimplemented!()`, `todo!()`, `panic!()`, or a dummy empty result in any public decompile path that the tests call after compile/serialize/uncompile. Do not roll back a verbose but complete decompile implementation to a compiling stub during repair. Do not rely on moving local helper records out of a table if the same record must be reused for multiple bypass paths.
rules.risk: The automaton can compile, match, serialize, and uncompile correctly but still fail when the test performs DFA -> regex -> parse -> compile. Repairs often then fail compilation because local Arrow-like records are moved, cloned without a Clone implementation, or compared by enum casts with precedence errors.
rules.guidance: Implement a local state-elimination algorithm: create an extra sentinel start/final slot, add epsilon arrows from the sentinel to the real initial state and from accepting states to the sentinel, group all byte transitions between each state pair into a symbol-set label, then repeatedly eliminate a real state by composing incoming, self-loop, and outgoing arrows and unioning with any existing arrow. Represent missing arrows explicitly with Option or an empty helper constructor. If a local helper struct or enum is stored in a Vec/table and reused, derive or implement Clone for that local helper; if precedence ordering is needed, derive PartialOrd/Ord on the local enum or parenthesize every enum cast comparison. Parenthesize comparisons such as `(prec as u8) < other_prec as u8`. Keep full-byte loops in a non-overflowing form such as `0u16..256` or `0..=u8::MAX`. A compile fix for this callable must preserve a real returned regex; if ownership or precedence errors are hard, simplify the labels or clone helper records, but never replace the body with `unimplemented!()`/`todo!()` or an empty string just to satisfy the compiler.

rules.title: Make mutating sequence entrypoints change length and order
rules.trigger: A public vector/list/splice/remove/swap-remove callable mutates a sequence by start index, count, or capacity.
rules.goal: Preserve the caller-visible length and element order changes instead of returning a successful no-op.
rules.constraint: Do not leave a mutating entrypoint with an empty body, a dummy success return, or only a capacity check when the C operation removes, shifts, swaps, truncates, or compacts elements. Do not add Copy or Clone bounds to an unconstrained public generic mutator just to move elements.
rules.risk: The crate can compile and many independent vector helpers can pass, but splice-style tests still see the original length because the translated mutator did nothing. A repair that uses slice::copy_within on Vec<T> can also fail compilation because copy_within requires T: Copy.
